title: Hazard-Ratio Comparison of Unlearning Methods Under Relearning Pressure

original_idea.body:
# Hazard-Ratio Comparison of Unlearning Methods

**Problem:** Unlearning methods are compared on single-point metrics, ignoring resistance to adversarial relearning over time.

**Direction:** Fit a Cox model with method as covariate, relearning examples as time, knowledge-recovered as event; estimate a hazard ratio between two methods.

**Why it matters:** A rigorous comparative durability metric.

**Relevant context:** arXiv:2505.16831; arXiv:2510.02712; arXiv:2501.04952.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Comparative durability metric for unlearning targets the dangerous-knowledge pathway recognized as critical.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Two unlearning methods plus relearning fine-tunes and Cox fit; guided.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Focused hazard-ratio comparison; depends on two unlearning setups and relearning runs.

counterfactual_value.reasoning: Neglected long-horizon dangerous-knowledge auditing benefiting from external comparison.

low_compute.reasoning: Two unlearning procedures plus small relearning fine-tunes on one GPU.

novelty.reasoning: Closely related to gen-2014; Cox-based comparative durability framing may be partly open.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Relearning reversal known; comparative hazard-ratio framing may be open.
